reference: No GNU command-line utility implements this Bash loadable. Runnable expectations use Bash's documented type/help builtin behavior and the maintained setpgid contract in docs/sol-setpgid.md; they do not invoke the setpgid operation. POSIX setpgid(2) and independent getpgid/getsid observations are specified as future operation oracles in the deferred cases.
coverage: Bash identifies setpgid as a builtin through type -t and type.
Bash help exposes the documented setpgid synopsis, exact operand count and zero-ID semantics.
Bash help exposes the documented ID bounds and same-session/session-leader restrictions.
Future isolated operation coverage is specified for owned-child success, argument validation and kernel-rejected process states.
exclusions: There is no matching GNU CLI, so no fake command-line parity oracle is used.
No setpgid operation is invoked here: changing process-group membership is outside the authorized metadata-only execution scope.
The deferred cases are not passes and do not validate runtime syscall behavior, errno wording or cross-platform pid_t width.

cases.purpose: Check Bash type metadata reports the available loadable as a builtin.
Check Bash's type description identifies setpgid as a shell builtin, independently of any external executable search path.
cases.script: description=$(type setpgid); [[ $description == *'setpgid is a shell builtin'* ]] && printf 'builtin-description-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check help -s renders the builtin's declared usage synopsis, including both required operands.
Check help describes nonnegative pid_t IDs, the zero defaults, and the documented same-session/session-leader limits.
cases.script: documentation=$(help setpgid); [[ $documentation == *'numeric process identifier, >= 0'* && $documentation == *'numeric process group identifier, >=0'* && $documentation == *'Zero pid selects the calling process.'* && $documentation == *'For zero pgrpid, the new process group ID is the target process ID.'* && $documentation == *'IDs must fit pid_t.'* && $documentation == *'The target must be in the caller'* && $documentation == *'cannot be a session leader.'* ]] && printf 'id-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise successful default and explicit process-group changes and verify the resulting group after each change.
Verify exact arity, numeric/nonnegative parsing and pid_t range rejection without changing process-group state.
Verify kernel error handling for a missing/reaped or nonchild PID, an unavailable group, a session leader, and an executed child.
